title: Local-to-global smoothing of proper nodal curves
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C/k$ a connected projective reduced curve whose only singularities are $d$ ordinary nodes, labelled $q_1,\ldots,q_d$, with completed local rings $k[[x,y]]/(xy)$. Assume that $C$ has no infinitesimal automorphisms: every $k$-derivation of $\mathcal O_C$ into itself is zero. For an Artinian local $k$-algebra $R$ with residue field $k$, let $\operatorname{Def}_C(R)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of flat proper $R$-curves with an identification of their special fibre with $C$; isomorphisms must preserve that identification. The functor $\operatorname{Def}_C$ is prorepresented by a formally smooth complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra, with tangent space $\operatorname{Ext}^1_C(\Omega_{C/k},\mathcal O_C)$. Restriction to completed local rings gives a formally smooth map from this deformation functor to the product of the $d$ local node-deformation functors. Each local node functor has hull $k[[s_i]]$ with family $xy=s_i$. The relative tangent dimension of this map is $\dim_k\operatorname{Ext}^1_C(\Omega_{C/k},\mathcal O_C)-d$. Consequently its representing ring is a power series ring over $k[[s_1,\ldots,s_d]]$ in that many additional variables, with the indicated local smoothing equations. If $C$ is a stable unpointed genus-$g$ curve, $g\geq2$, in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], it has no infinitesimal automorphisms and this Ext dimension is $3g-3$. For an effective proper nodal family over the representing complete local base, the locus of nonsmooth fibres is exactly the union of the loci $s_i=0$; there are no additional discriminant components. Formal smoothness here means lifting over every surjection of Artinian local algebras with square-zero kernel, and prorepresentation means natural bijections with continuous local homomorphisms from the stated complete local ring. Power series and completion are [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; $\Omega_{C/k}$ is the sheaf representing $k$-derivations and Ext is the derived Hom of coherent modules. The local node-deformation functor at $q_i$ takes $R$ to isomorphism classes of complete Noetherian local flat $R$-algebras with identified special fibre $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,q_i}$, with continuous isomorphisms preserving this identification. The statement is existential in the choices of the maps from the local hulls to the global representing ring; it does not assert that the local node functors themselves are prorepresented. Arithmetic genus is $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, as specified for stable families in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Differentials and Ext use [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-ext-sheaf], properness and flatness use [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism], projectivity uses [def-kun-projective], and reducedness uses [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

source.place: Section 1, Lemmas 1.3--1.4, Proposition 1.5, Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.9, printed pp.79--83; equal-characteristic restriction. Dimension 3g-3 also as in Pikaart--de Jong 2.3.6. Local PDFs WANTED; primary PDFs read online.

proof.text: The curve is smooth away from the listed nodes; on that smooth open the last clause of the cotangent presentation theorem gives $L_{C/k}\simeq\Omega_{C/k}[0]$ with $\Omega_{C/k}$ locally free. At a node, the nodal point criterion gives an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $S$ a local complete intersection over $k$, so a principal open $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ containing the node is $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ with dimension $n-c$. Over the field $k$ this is a relative global complete intersection, so the $f_j$ form a regular sequence in every localization of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ at a prime containing them, hence a Koszul-regular sequence there. The Koszul homology modules are finitely generated and commute with localization, so they vanish after inverting one polynomial not in that prime; on that open of $\mathbf A^n_k$ the ideal is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence. There the cotangent complex is $[I/I^2\to\Omega_P\otimes\mathcal O_C]$ with both terms finite locally free. Its differential is injective: it is injective at the generic points, where $C/k$ is smooth, and a section of a free module over a reduced ring that vanishes at every minimal prime is zero (each coordinate belongs to the intersection of the minimal primes, which is the nilradical). Thus the canonical augmentation is an isomorphism $L_{C/k}\simeq\Omega_{C/k}[0]$ in the derived category. In particular $\Omega_{C/k}$ has locally a finite locally free resolution of length at most one. The reducedness assumption is essential for the injectivity argument.

source.place: Tags 0C4D and 0C4E; cotangent local presentation; Deligne--Mumford p.79, before Lemma 1.3

proof.text: Apply the proper-scheme hull theorem to $C$. The assumed vanishing of derivations upgrades its hull to a representing complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra $A$. By step 1 its tangent space is $\operatorname{Ext}^1_C(\Omega_{C/k},\mathcal O_C)$; write its finite dimension as $N$. The curve is separated, finite type, of dimension one, a local complete intersection, and smooth outside finitely many points. The isolated-lci unobstructedness theorem therefore applies, with coefficient ring $k$: every deformation lifts over an Artinian surjection. The properness-reflection theorem makes the lift proper, since the kernel of reduction to the special fibre is nilpotent. The complete-local smoothness theorem, applied to $k\to A$, now gives $A\cong k[[t_1,\ldots,t_N]]$. This proves absolute formal smoothness and prorepresentation, with the claimed tangent space.

For one node set $B_0=k[[x,y]]/(xy)$. The hypersurface presentation lemma writes each Artinian deformation as $R[[x,y]]/(F)$ with $F\bmod\mathfrak m_R=xy$, compatibly with a specified reduction isomorphism. Induct on the length of $R$, factoring a surjection into small extensions with kernel $J$ annihilated by the maximal ideal. If a reduced presentation is $xy-s$, lift its coordinates and $s$. The lifted equation is $xy-s+g$ with $g\in J[[x,y]]$. Write $g=c+xa+yb$ with $c\in J$ and $a,b\in J[[x,y]]$. Changing coordinates to $x+b,y+a$ removes $xa+yb$, since $J^2=0$; replacing $s$ by $s-c$ removes the constant. The coordinate changes have inverses modulo $J$ and preserve the chosen special fibre. Thus this construction lifts any specified map from the one-parameter family across a small extension. All equations $xy-s$ are flat by the converse of the presentation lemma. For dual numbers, the change-of-coordinates formula identifies the tangent space with $k[[x,y]]/(xy,x,y)=k$, and the constant perturbation $xy-\epsilon$ spans it. Hence $h_{k[[s]]}\to\operatorname{Def}_{B_0}$ is smooth and tangent bijective, precisely a hull. No uniqueness of $s$ over general Artinian bases is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0DY5 proof (2); explicit mixed-term induction as in Deligne--Mumford p.81, node example

proof.text: Choose $C=U\cup V$ using the isolated-curve two-affine-cover lemma, with every $q_i$ in $V$, and with $U$ and $U\cap V$ smooth affine. Fix a surjection $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$, a deformation $Y/R$ of $C$, and prescribed completed node deformations over $R'$ with specified identifications over $R$. The affine-thickening theorem makes $Y_V$ affine; its coordinate algebra is finite type over $R$ since $Y$ is proper. The completed-isolated-affine comparison applied to $V$ produces an affine deformation of $Y_V$ over $R'$ realizing all prescribed completions, together with the compatible reduction isomorphism. The smooth-open deformation gluing lemma extends this deformation of $Y_V$ to a flat deformation of all of $C$, respecting that isomorphism. The properness-reflection theorem for nilpotent base change makes this deformation proper. Its finite-type affine charts over the Noetherian Artinian base are finitely presented by the Noetherian finite-presentation theorem, so it is a deformation in the stated proper-flat functor. Its node completions are the prescribed ones. This proves formal smoothness of the restriction map, including compatibility with a chosen deformation over $R$, not merely existence of some lifting of $C$.

source.place: Tags 0DZP proof, 0DZF composite completed comparison, and 0DZN; properness under Artinian deformation

proof.text: Compute the sheaf Ext groups from the resolution in step 1. They vanish in degrees above one and in positive degrees on the smooth locus. At a node, the formal differential presentation and faithful flatness of local completion give the exact completed resolution $0\to B_0\xrightarrow{a\mapsto(ay,ax)}B_0^2\to\widehat\Omega_{C/k,q_i}\to0$. The left arrow is injective because an element annihilated by both $x$ and $y$ is zero. Dualizing gives cokernel $B_0/(x,y)=k$. Finite free dual matrices commute with flat completion, so this computes the completed local Ext; faithful flatness detects the vanishing assertions, and the completed Ext module $k$ descends to the residue module $k$ (its maximal ideal acts by zero, and its dimension is one). By the sheaf-Ext stalk identification, $\mathcal Ext^1(\Omega_{C/k},\mathcal O_C)\cong\bigoplus_i k_{q_i}$. In degree zero put $T_C=\mathcal Hom(\Omega_{C/k},\mathcal O_C)$. All these sheaves are coherent.

source.place: Completed split-node calculation; Tag 0CBW; Deligne--Mumford pp.79,81--82

proof.text: The sheaf-Ext local-to-global spectral sequence has only rows $q=0,1$. The terms $H^p(C,T_C)$ vanish for $p>1$ by dimension-one cohomological vanishing, and the positive cohomology of the coherent zero-dimensional-support sheaf $\bigoplus_i k_{q_i}$ vanishes. Reading the total-degree-one edge and the possible outgoing differential to $H^2(C,T_C)=0$ therefore gives the exact sequence $0\to H^1(C,T_C)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_C(\Omega_{C/k},\mathcal O_C)\to\bigoplus_i k\to0$. It also gives $\operatorname{Ext}^2_C(\Omega_{C/k},\mathcal O_C)=0$. The edge map is restriction of extensions to the local stalks followed by completion, hence is the tangent map of step 4 under the natural tangent identification in the proper-scheme deformation theorem and the computation of step 3. Consequently the relative tangent dimension is $N-d$, and $d\leq N$.

source.place: Tag 0BQP (local-to-global Ext) and Tag 02UZ; coherent.tex Tag 0B3J; Deligne--Mumford Lemma 1.3 and Proposition 1.5

proof.text: For each $n$ choose a representative of the universal class over $A/\mathfrak m_A^n$. Successive reductions have equal classes by prorepresentation, so choose reduction isomorphisms and compose them to obtain a compatible tower starting at $C$. At each node, step 3 and the compatible-tower presentation lemma choose local equations $xy-s_{i,n}$ and compatible coordinate isomorphisms at successive orders. Thus $s_i=\varprojlim_n s_{i,n}\in A$ and the completed formal local family is $A[[x,y]]/(xy-s_i)$. The linear classes of the $s_i$ are independent in $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2$, because their dual map is the surjective tangent map of step 6. Extend them to a basis by $u_1,\ldots,u_{N-d}$. Under the power series presentation from step 2 this ordered list is a full regular system of parameters. The full-coordinate theorem for power series over any field therefore identifies $A$ with $k[[s_1,\ldots,s_d,u_1,\ldots,u_{N-d}]]$, preserving every $s_i$. This is the required power series extension of the product local hull $k[[s_1,\ldots,s_d]]$, with the indicated equations.

source.place: Tag 07NM (lemma-quotient-power-series-ring-over-Cohen), part (1); compatible node normal forms of step 3

proof.text: Now assume $C$ is stable and unpointed of arithmetic genus $g\geq2$. On each normalized component $C_a$, let $g_a$ be its genus and $b_a$ its number of nodal branches. Stability says $b_a\geq3$ if $g_a=0$, $b_a\geq1$ if $g_a=1$, and imposes no extra condition when $g_a\geq2$; in every case $2g_a-2+b_a>0$. Apply the marked nodal infinitesimal-vector-field theorem with no markings: its normalized fixed-point conditions are exactly these branch points, and its final inequality gives that the infinitesimal automorphism group is trivial. An automorphism of $\mathcal O_C[\epsilon]$ over $k[\epsilon]$ that is the identity modulo $\epsilon$ is $a\mapsto a+\epsilon D(a)$ with $D$ a $k$-derivation of $\mathcal O_C$, and every such $D$ gives one; so this group is $\operatorname{Der}_k(\mathcal O_C,\mathcal O_C)=H^0(C,T_C)$, which is therefore $0$. Thus the no-infinitesimal-automorphisms assumption is automatic in this stable case, in every characteristic.

Use the completed-normalization-model theorem to obtain the finite normalization $\nu:\widetilde C\to C$, its smooth projective components, its isomorphism off the nodes and its two branch points over each node. At a node, that theorem verifies all hypotheses of the local derivation-descent lemma. That lemma identifies the stalk of $T_C$ with derivations on the semilocal normalization vanishing at both branch points. On the smooth locus restriction is the identity. The extension maps commute with localization and are unique, so these stalk descriptions glue to mutually inverse sheaf maps $T_C\cong\nu_*T_{\widetilde C}(-E)$, where $E$ is the reduced inverse image of the nodes. On a smooth curve vanishing at a point is exactly divisibility of the local vector field by a uniformizer, giving the divisor twist $-E$. Thus this sheaf identification follows from the existing local theorem; it is not a new lemma requiring a duplicate node.

source.place: Tag 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields), local argument; source completed-normalization hypotheses are explicit in the two cited nodes

proof.text: Let $v$ be the number of normalized components. The tangent-sheaf normalization isomorphism of step 9 and the cohomology edge isomorphism for the finite, hence affine, normalization give $\chi(C,T_C)=\sum_a\chi(C_a,T_{C_a}(-E_a))$, where $E_a$ is the reduced branch divisor of degree $b_a$ and $\sum_a b_a=2d$, including self-nodes. On the smooth proper component, canonical degree and Riemann--Roch give $\deg T_{C_a}(-E_a)=2-2g_a-b_a$ and $\chi(T_{C_a}(-E_a))=3-3g_a-b_a$. Hence $-\chi(C,T_C)=\sum_a(3g_a-3)+2d$. The nodal normalization Euler formula gives $1-g=v-d-\sum_a g_a$, so this is $3g-3-d$. Since $H^0(C,T_C)=0$ by step 8 and higher cohomology vanishes by step 6, $\dim H^1(C,T_C)=3g-3-d$. Adding the $d$ local directions in the exact sequence of step 6 yields $N=3g-3$.

source.place: Tag 0E68 local vector fields; normalization Euler formula; Riemann--Roch and canonical degree on smooth components

proof.text: Finally let an effective proper nodal family $\mathscr C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ inducing the universal formal deformation be given. Its first-Fitting singular subscheme $Z$ is supported exactly where the morphism is nonsmooth, is unramified over $A$, and commutes with base change. The closed-immersion properness theorem makes it proper over $A$. The unramified-quasi-finite theorem makes it locally quasi-finite, and properness supplies quasi-compactness; thus it is quasi-finite. The proper-quasi-finite theorem makes $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ finite. Its closed fibre consists precisely of the $d$ reduced nodes. At $q_i$, step 7 gives the completed equation $xy-s_i$. The completed relative differential module is presented by the column $(y,x)$, so its first Fitting ideal is $(x,y)$; the completed local ring of $Z$ at $q_i$ is therefore $A[[x,y]]/(xy-s_i,x,y)=A/(s_i)$. This uses relative differentials over $A$, so no $\mathrm ds_i$ term occurs.

source.place: Tags 0C59 and 0C5B; relative Jacobian/Fitting computation as in Deligne--Mumford Corollary 1.9

proof.text: Write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S$ with $S$ finite over $A$. Apply the finite-extension completion formula at the maximal ideal of $A$. Since $A$ is complete, its left-hand side is $S$, and its right-hand side is the product of the completed local rings at the points of the closed fibre, which are exactly the $q_i$. Thus $S\cong\prod_i A/(s_i)$ as an $A$-algebra. Its image in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is exactly $\bigcup_i V(s_i)$. By step 11 this image is precisely the locus with a nonsmooth fibre, proving that there are no additional discriminant components. If $d=0$, the product is the zero ring, so $Z$ is empty and every fibre is smooth. All earlier formulas also permit $d=0$, with an empty product of local deformation functors and relative tangent dimension $N$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-ND-545d3fd09 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Fourth push of this split. Heads 9e8a, 1b5d and 08a2 were all FIXes; each was refused at landing because the side completion was never promoted, never on the mathematics. This head is identical to 08a2: the 4 new nodes are byte-identical and the item differs only in split_report date/summary. There is no repair note and no SGA citation. So the 08a2 fixes were lost again; I re-applied them by splicing into this head and kept the new summary. I read all 12 steps and the 4 new nodes, and re-read every cited statement in this snapshot. (1) C4/E1, step 1: lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation needs a Koszul-regular presentation, which the nodal criterion alone does not give. The step now goes global ci, then relative global ci, then a local regular sequence (lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence), then Koszul-regular (lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular), on an open of A^n; the smooth locus uses the theorem's smooth clause. proof_deps and tool_uses gain these two nodes, and proof_deps now equals the union of the steps' uses. (2) C4, step 8: lem-sfb-marked-nodal-infinitesimal-fields identifies the infinitesimal automorphisms with derivations on the normalization, not with Der_k(O_C), so the step now uses the elementary 1+εD argument. (3) B2: the last clause of lem-sfb-formal-hypersurface-deformation-presentation left its objects undefined. It is now stated for a finitely presented X→Spec R with Ô_{X,x}≅R[[x]]/(F), and three stmt_deps are added. Hand checks: step 3, (x+b)(y+a)=xy+xa+yb because J²=0, which also works in characteristic 2; step 5, Ext¹ is k; step 6, 0→H¹(T)→Ext¹→⊕k→0 and Ext²=0; step 10, −χ(T)=3g−3−d, so N=3g−3; steps 11–12, Fitt₁=(x,y), so S≅∏A/(s_i). New nodes match Stacks 0ET5/0DYA, 0DZF, 0DY5 and 06HL. Duplicate search on this base: lem-sfb-flat-space-split-deformation-ext covers only the hull's first-order tangent clause, and the curve-stack versality nodes concern algebraic stacks; neither is a duplicate. Batch-5 flags: every flagged citation (stable-curve definition, coherent Riemann–Roch and canonical degree, marked-nodal fields, lci cotangent complex, normalization Euler characteristic, Fitting singular locus, node criterion, completed differential presentation) is generic algebraic geometry, not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so all are accepted. Maintainer note: this is the fourth identical push; promote the side completion together with these fix files.; 2 file(s) fixed by the reviewer

lean.statement: theorem exists_smoothing (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) [C.Over (Spec (.of k))] [ConnectedSpace C] [IsReduced C] [IsHProjective (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] [HasExt.{u} C.Modules] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (d : ℕ) (q : Fin d → C) (hq : Function.Injective q) (hsmooth : ∀ x : C, x ∉ Set.range q → ∃ U : C.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ (C ↘ Spec (.of k)))) (eq : ∀ i : Fin d, Completed (C.presheaf.stalk (q i)) ≃+* Node k) (eq_scalar : ∀ (i : Fin d) (a : k), eq i (algebraMap _ _ (stalkScalar (C ↘ Spec (.of k)) (q i) a)) = algebraMap k _ a) : (Subsingleton ((C ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials ⟶ Scheme.Modules.unit C) → FiniteDimensional k (Scheme.Modules.Ext (C ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials (Scheme.Modules.unit C) 1) ∧ Nonempty (Smoothing d (Module.finrank k (Scheme.Modules.Ext (C ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials (Scheme.Modules.unit C) 1)) q eq)) ∧ (∀ (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (M : StablePointedModuli.Fiber (Spec (.of k)) g 0 (Over.mk (𝟙 _))), Nonempty (StablePointedModuli.fiberCurve M ≅ Over.mk (C ↘ Spec (.of k))) → Subsingleton ((C ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials ⟶ Scheme.Modules.unit C) ∧ Module.finrank k (Scheme.Modules.Ext (C ↘ Spec (.of k)).relativeDifferentials (Scheme.Modules.unit C) 1) = 3 * g - 3)
